skill: Convert a positive numeric nth root to the same base raised to the unit fraction 1/n, recognizing implicit index 2.
learner_operation: Identify radicand x and index n (2 for an unindexed square root), preserve x as base, and select x^(1/n) among competing assignments of base, numerator and denominator.
reasoning_steps: Read radicand and explicit or implicit root index.
Discriminate the equivalent expression from swapped-role or inverted-exponent distractors.
response_contract: Observed questions use one radio selection with five mathematical choices. Canonical worked example gives an expression but supplies no answer field.
difficulty: easy; one substitution into a notation conversion rule, without powers in the radicand, arithmetic simplification, negative values, or reverse conversion.
invariants: Positive integer radicand and integer root index at least 2.
Single correct selection; five choices for observed question families.
Worked solution states the identity, identifies x and n, and substitutes them.
permitted_variations: Positive integer radicand and index may change independently where choices remain distinct.
Implicit square root and explicit higher-index roots.
Correct choice position and distractor ordering may change.
Answer-bearing base and denominator must track changes to x and n; no source example fixes their numeric assignments.
Distractor profiles may follow the three observed complete banks; corrected malformed TeX is permissible.
essential_vs_incidental: The exponent numerator 1 and retention of radicand as base are essential mathematics. Particular bases 2, 5, 10 and indices 7, 3, 2, answer UUIDs and positions are incidental. Choosing the only unit fraction, if the answer bank allows it without reading the radical, would be an incidental shortcut; distinguishing x^(1/n) from n^(1/x) is intended reasoning.
